unitemized.reason: This API naming standard only applies if the task defines REST endpoints. That condition can't be written as a predicate, and no kind inspects endpoint names in code or the spec.
This only applies if the task involves nested resource URLs. That condition can't be written as a predicate, and no kind counts URL nesting depth.
This only applies if the task creates database tables. That condition can't be written as a predicate, and no kind inspects schema definitions.
This only applies if the change writes database queries. That condition can't be written as a predicate, and no kind scans the diff content for SELECT *.
This is a soft preference ("Prefer") that only applies to CSS work. That condition can't be written as a predicate, and no kind inspects the CSS units in the diff.
This only applies to mobile UI work. Tap target size is a rendered property that the trace and diff kinds can't check.
This is a general style guideline about consistent formatting. It is a matter of judgment, and no kind runs a formatter or checks the diff's formatting.
This naming guideline has a vague exception ("except in narrow contexts"). It is a matter of judgment, and no kind inspects identifiers in the diff.
Indentation consistency in the diff can't be checked with any of the available kinds. The 'configure your editor/linter' part is outside what the run can observe.
Whether an exception type is 'specific' enough is a matter of judgment, and no kind inspects which exception types the diff uses.
'Fast (milliseconds)' is a soft target for the project's unit tests, and no kind measures how long a test takes to run.
This is an implicit statement of where the documents are located. Reading from /agent-os is already covered by the cw-003 doc_read items, and no write rule follows from it.
